title: MOVE operand serialisation drops subscripts, qualifiers and LENGTH OF
description: The ASG cache is written as json.dumps(asg.to_dict()) (cobble/cobble/parsing/parse_corpus.py:99), so every operand field the to_dict side omits is lost before any later stage reads it. MoveStatement._operand_dict (cobol_asg/cobol_statements.py:165) emits only name, ref_mod_start and ref_mod_length, while RefModOperand (cobol_asg/ref_mod.py:145) also carries subscripts, qualifiers, length_of and rounded, and from_dict reads all of them. ComputeTarget.to_dict serialises subscripts, so MOVE is inconsistent with its neighbour. Effect: a cache built with the current jar still has zero subscripted MOVE operands, and MOVE is the highest-volume verb in the corpus. A LENGTH OF source is worse than lossy -- it round-trips to an operand with an empty name. Refines 8y0, which correctly cleared the bridge and stopped one layer too early: the serialiser between bridge and cache is the culprit, and the stale cache masked it.
design: Serialise the full RefModOperand from _operand_dict, following ComputeTarget.to_dict's shape (emit each optional field only when set, so unsubscripted operands keep their current compact form and existing fixtures stay valid). Round-trip test: a subscripted operand and a LENGTH OF operand must survive to_dict then from_dict unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: to_dict/from_dict round-trip preserves subscripts, qualifiers, length_of and rounded on MOVE operands; unsubscripted operands serialise byte-identically to before; red-dragon suite green.
close_reason: Fixed upstream in red-dragon d07c3581 (MOVE operands keep their subscripts through to_dict), merged into forge via the submodule bump on main. Confirmed by the re-parse: the rebuilt cache carries 102,922 subscripted MOVE operands where the old one carried 0, with total and ref_modified byte-identical.

title: [bug] Bridge drops subscripts on MOVE operands: the interpreter silently reads and writes row 1 of every table
description:
MOVE is the only statement whose operands lose their subscripts. The source

    MOVE WS-MSG-LINE (WS-IDX) TO MSG-OUT

arrives as

    {"type": "MOVE", "operands": [{"name": "WS-MSG-LINE"}, {"name": "MSG-OUT"}]}

with (WS-IDX) silently gone. RefModOperand.from_dict already reads a "subscripts"
key and expr_from_dict already parses the nodes, so the Python side is ready; the
Java bridge simply does not emit them for MOVE. It does emit them elsewhere --
counted over 60 cached ASGs, subscripts appear under IF 958 times, PERFORM 50,
SEARCH 41, ADD 20, WHEN 5, and under MOVE exactly 0.

MEASURED COST, 300 programs, from the dataflow spike:
  114,448 references resolve to a table item with no subscript to place it
   91,602 MOVEs (19% of 492,405) therefore degrade to a weak update, unioning
          provenance into every row of the table instead of writing one

Weak updates are correct but they are the coarsest answer available, and they are
being forced by missing data rather than by genuine uncertainty. The distinction
matters most exactly where the corpus uses it: WS-MSG-LINE(WS-IDX) is a variable
subscript and has to widen, but SCR-CODE(3) and WS-FLAGS(1) are literal and must
not -- and cobble/dataflow/layout.py already materialises every occurrence with an
`index` tuple precisely so a literal subscript lands on one cell. None of that
precision is reachable until the bridge emits the operand.

Fix is Java-side in proleap-bridge: emit "subscripts" on MOVE operands the way the
condition and arithmetic paths already do. Then re-run the spike and the weak-update
count should drop to the genuinely-variable subscripts only.

Repro: grep any ONLINE program for a subscripted MOVE (PROG-B5:215, PROG-B1:1530,
PROG-B6:1306) and compare against the MOVE node in its ASG.
notes: Redacted 2026-09-07: corpus program, file, field and paragraph names replaced with stable pseudonyms (PROG-*, FILE-*, MST-*, SCR-*, BUF-*, LAY-*, MSG-*). Measured numbers and source line references are unchanged. The mapping and the pre-redaction text are in .knowledge_graph_scratch/ (untracked, per-machine).
close_reason:
NOT A BUG -- retracted. My evidence was a stale ASG cache, not the current bridge.

serializeMoveOperand (StatementSerializer.java:2183) is a one-line delegate to
serializeRef, the unified structured-reference serializer that emits "subscripts"
whenever non-empty. Commit 1a99c445 "feat(bridge): emit structured subscripts (bare
name + all subscripts), retire flattening (red-dragon-6ddr)" landed exactly this, and
57cf80e9 then retired _SUBSCRIPT_RE / parse_subscript_notation on the Python side
because subscripts had become fully structural. The lowering consumes them at
lower_arithmetic.py:419,436.

My cached ASGs were generated before 6ddr, so every MOVE in them has bare operands.
The "interpreter reads row 1 of every table" claim does not hold and the P0 was wrong.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DATAFLOW SPIKE: its subscript numbers are worthless and must be
rediscovered against a rebuilt cache. Specifically these were cache artifacts, not
corpus properties:
  114,448 references to table items with no subscript
   91,602 MOVEs degraded to weak updates (19%)
Rebuild the cache with the current jar and re-run before quoting any of them.

comments.author: Avishek Sen Gupta
comments.text:
SEVERITY ESCALATION -- this is not an analysis limitation, it is a silent
wrong-answer bug in the interpreter.

The IR lowering already asks for MOVE subscripts and already knows what to do with
them. interpreter/cobol/lower_arithmetic.py, lower_move at 351:

    419:                    subscripts=target.subscripts,
    436:            subscripts=stmt.source.subscripts,

and emit_context.py resolve_field_ref handles them properly -- 1-D via
"(idx-1)*stride + base", multi-D by accumulating per-dimension OCCURS strides
(red-dragon-1wy3), with an explicit error when the subscript count exceeds the
declared dimensions.

But emit_context.py:263 reads:

    if not subscripts:

and falls through to the base FieldLayout. The bridge hands MOVE an empty subscript
tuple, so that branch is always taken. Consequence:

    MOVE WS-MSG-LINE (WS-IDX) TO MSG-OUT

lowers to a LoadRegion at WS-MSG-LINE's base offset with no index arithmetic emitted
at all. The interpreter reads row 1. Every subscripted MOVE in every program reads
and writes row 1 of the table, silently -- no error, no warning, no diagnostic.
the corpus uses subscripted MOVE constantly (PROG-B5:215, PROG-B1:1530/1575/2269/2370-75),
so any the corpus online transaction that indexes a table is executing against the wrong row.

Other verbs are unaffected because the bridge does emit their subscripts: counted over
the cached ASGs, IF 958, PERFORM 50, SEARCH 41, ADD 20, WHEN 5, MOVE 0.

WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT: tests/unit/cobol/test_ref_mod_operand_subscripts.py and
test_resolve_field_ref_subscripts.py both hand-construct the dicts they feed to
RefModOperand.from_dict. They prove the Python half parses subscripts and the lowering
half consumes them. Neither crosses the Java seam, so the one thing that is broken --
the bridge not emitting them for MOVE -- is exactly the thing untested.

Regression test to add alongside the fix: parse a source containing a subscripted MOVE
through the real bridge and assert the operand's subscripts are non-empty. An
end-to-end execution test that MOVEs into row 3 and reads row 3 back would also fail
today.

title: cobble-viz-sequence marks PERFORMs under an EVALUATE WHEN as simple, not conditional
description: sequence_cmd.py _determine_call_type only checks '.then.'/'.else.' in the CALL node id; srccfg ids WHEN arms as '<stmt>.when.<n>.<k>'. COACTVWC 0000-MAIN: 2000-PROCESS-INPUTS (0000-MAIN/9.when.2.0) and SEND-PLAIN-TEXT (9.when.3.4) are published as 'simple' though each runs only in one WHEN arm. Deck impact: docs/presentation/artifacts/cobble/viz/COACTVWC-sequence-program.png (regenerated JSON is identical to the published one, so this is current code).
close_reason: Steps carry the arms (IF then/else, EVALUATE when.<n>) read from the site's node path; any arm makes the call conditional. Renderer draws arms as Mermaid alt/else blocks. Deck artifacts regenerated.

title: cobble srccfg: EVALUATE FALSE WHEN guards are not negated
description: conditions.py:321 _CONDITION_SUBJECTS treats FALSE like TRUE. EVALUATE FALSE WHEN WS-A = 1 yields guard 'WS-A = 1' instead of NOT(WS-A = 1), inverting the arm's reaching condition.
close_reason: EVALUATE FALSE WHEN guards are now wrapped in Not (WHEN OTHER stays ALWAYS). Tests in tests/dataflow/srccfg/test_conditions.py.

title: cobble-fields-trace LINK-return bridge rows attribute caller-origin sources to the callee
description: trace.py:828-841: _seeded rebases destinations but keeps sources pointing into the caller; _bridge labels them source_program=frame.program (callee). Caller MOVE WS-IN TO WS-COMM, LINK, callee untouched -> row 'CALLER WS-COMM <- WS-IN@working_storage[0:4]' with source_program=CALLEE. Backward trace-query then follows unrelated callee storage (the confusion 0a84fd4f aimed to fix). Same mis-programmed extent passed to _definers(callee_state) at :835.
close_reason: Bridge rows now take source_program and definer store from the program that read the source (qualified Source.node prefix). Severity lower than filed: the LINK statement's own transfer kills caller provenance in an EXACT window, so on real input the visible symptom was the %CALL origin row duplicated under both programs; storage pass-through only survives a non-killing transfer write. Tests: test_a_bridge_row_names_the_program_its_source_was_read_in, test_a_passed_through_sources_definers_are_read_in_its_own_programs_storage.

title: cobble-fields-trace stops sampling while stale plans remain, under-covering CICS handler arms
description: trace.py:1136-1146 terminates when the fresh lane empties. Arms at non-test decisions (e.g. CICS raise/handler arms from c6a26692) have no coverage key and are always filed stale (_filed, :473), so they are never sampled and reported as structurally unreachable. Contradicts _Queue docstring 'nothing is ever dropped'. Repro: non-test decision whose two arms each lead to a test -> stops after 2 paths at 2/4 branches with 1 stale plan queued.
close_reason: Plans whose flip has no branch-coverage key go to a new 'uncounted' lane drained after fresh; the run stops only when stale alone remains. Stop reason reworded (ONLY_STALE) to drop the false 'structurally unreachable' claim. Test: test_a_flip_at_a_decision_coverage_does_not_count_is_walked_before_stopping.

title: cobble.viz has no tests
description: cobble/tests/viz/ contains only __init__.py. None of the four viz commands is exercised, which let the LINK/hardcoded-corpus bugs ship. Add tests against real upstream output shapes (edges.jsonl, cfg-*.json, trace.jsonl).

description: bms_render.py:72-83 draws an OCCURS=n field once. BNK1ACC ACCOUNT (OCCURS=10, rows 9-18) fills row 9 only.

title: cobble BMS: doubled quotes / ampersands in INITIAL are never un-escaped
description: bms_metadata.py:56-62 _strip_quotes only removes outer quotes; hlasm_export passes raw operands. COUSR00 renders "Type ''U'' to Update" (also in the message field's screen_label). Length is measured on the raw text, so 'A&&B' truncates to 'A&'. Used by bms_render.py:80.

title: Bridge dep rows lose the callee's program, so backward queries stop at the LINK and can invent flows
description:
778a7de0 made _handed_back emit bridge Deps whose source is a callee-space extent. Two things are wrong downstream.

The JSONL row carries one `program` field and _extent_dict carries none, so trace_query._dep_of stamps the caller's program onto the source ByteRange. ByteRange._comparable requires equal programs, so the backward frontier (CALLER, region, callee_start, callee_end) never matches the callee's own rows (CALLEE, ...) -- the walk gains one hop and still cannot reach the callee's writes, which is the thing the fix set out to do. Worse, that frontier CAN match an unrelated caller field at the same offsets, inventing a flow; the trace is sound one way only and is allowed to miss flows, not fabricate them.

_bridge also passes via=walk.via while walk.stack still holds the crossing frame, so a row whose program is the caller claims the caller was entered through its own call site. Dep's docstring says via is empty in the program the trace started from.
acceptance_criteria: An end-to-end test (trace -> trace_report JSONL -> trace_query backward) reaches a definer inside the callee, and no bridge row reports a via for the start program.
notes: Confirmed by running the query over the row shape the fix produces: the walk stops at the bridge row, and with an unrelated caller field at the same offsets it walks into that field's provenance instead.
close_reason: source_program added to Dep and the JSONL row; via computed from the resumed stack; _narrowed clipped to the overlap and _narrow_sources yields one slice per overlapping frontier range

title: fields trace: replace heuristic arm choice with systematic path enumeration
description:
The coverage-guided arm choice landed in c72da56 fixed path depth (61-99 nodes instead of 6) but not the coverage plateau: a 9181-node member freezes at 5% and the client member at 93/3140 over 400 paths. Measured cause: the backward frontier covers 9087 of 9181 nodes because the CFG is near-strongly-connected (788 PERFORM, 788 RETURN, 460 GOTO edges), so 'some untaken edge is still reachable from this arm' is true almost everywhere -- of 1247 two-arm decisions over 60 paths it discriminated 151 times and 808 fell through to the cursor. No local per-node rule can fix this, because a deep branch edge needs a specific combination of about twenty choices and independent per-node counters cannot enumerate combinations.

Replace the shape. A path becomes a choice sequence -- the arm index taken at each multi-arm decision, in order -- and the walk becomes a pure function of it. After a path, every recorded decision where taken + 1 < arms names an untried alternative plan (prefix + (taken + 1,)); the run keeps a FIFO queue of those, so shallow alternatives are explored before deep ones and no path is ever walked twice. An empty queue is exact exhaustion, replacing the over-approximate frontier claim.

Removes more than it adds: _Reach, _grown, _frontier, _is_test, _unexplored, _with_frontier, the per-node cursors, and the covered/frontiers fields all go.

Does not promise a coverage rate: a flipped arm can be an edge already taken under a different prefix. It removes the plateau's cause, which is what was asked for.
acceptance_criteria: Coverage on a large member keeps climbing rather than freezing; the exhaustion stop fires only when the choice queue is empty; the raise-chain, straight-line and unreachable-test fixtures still reach full coverage in depth+1, 3 and 2 paths.
close_reason: Shape change shipped: a path is a plan (the arm index at each decision), the walk is a pure function of it, and exhaustion is exact. Deleted _Reach, _grown, _frontier, _is_test, _unexplored, _with_frontier, the per-node cursors and the covered/frontiers fields; net smaller. Acceptance only partly met -- coverage climbs (207 at 100 paths, 355 at 2000, 521 at 40000) rather than freezing outright, but the treads are hundreds to thousands of paths long and the cause is structural, not a missing rule. That residual is red-dragon-forge-uik, re-scoped to it and raised to P2.

comments.author: Avishek Sen Gupta
comments.text:
Implemented and green (49 tests in the trace suite, 1245 in cobble, pyright 0, 11/11 import contracts, Black clean). Measured on a 9181-node/14007-edge member, budget vs branch edges taken:

  100 paths  207/6684 (3.1%)    4.0s
  500 paths  207/6684 (3.1%)    1.4s
 2000 paths  355/6980 (5.09%)   6.7s
10000 paths  355/6980 (5.09%)  42.2s
40000 paths  521/6980 (7.46%) 340.1s

Against the heuristic chooser's 336/6980 at 100 paths in 128s, this is ~400x cheaper per path and exactly terminating, but coverage per path is WORSE and the acceptance criterion is NOT met: the plateau became a staircase with very long flat treads rather than disappearing. 1866 of 2000 paths add zero new branch edges, and the two steps in the table coincide with the denominator changing -- they are new programs being entered, not new edges inside the member.

Root cause is structural, not a missing rule. Every alternative plan is the base route with ONE decision flipped, so consecutive paths overlap almost completely and the best case is about two new branch edges per path. 6684 branch edges therefore needs >3300 productive paths for one member, and one path in eight to fifteen is productive.

Drain order measured at a 2000-path budget: FIFO 355 edges (queue 22727), LIFO 153 (queue starves to 65 -- depth-first burrows into one corner), and a two-queue split that drains alternatives of productive routes ahead of alternatives of barren ones 578 (queue 17908). The split is a real 63% win and one field wide, but it is a heuristic on scheduling and does not change the order of magnitude, so it is deliberately not in this commit.

title: fields trace: sampling loses half its paths per desugared exception arm
description:
Measured on a 3919-node online member: of 400 sampled paths, 200 end after 6 nodes at the entry paragraph's first desugared CICS condition raise, 100 more end at the second, and 330/400 end at a '#dispatch' sink overall. Only 70 get past the entry paragraph. Branch coverage after 400 paths is 58/3102, and 200000 paths reached only 126/3140 -- the curve is flat because attrition is 2^-k in the number of raise sites on a route, so a deep route needs 1-in-1024 luck.

Cause: a desugared raise is a TEST whose TRUE arm targets a CALL node with no successors, and _sampled's per-node round-robin (edges[seen % len(edges)]) gives that arm half of every visit. The arm can only ever witness the one dispatch node, so every visit after the first buys nothing, yet it costs a whole path.

Fix direction: make arm choice coverage-guided -- thread the run's cumulative taken set into the walk beside the cursors it already threads, prefer an admissible arm not yet taken anywhere in the run, fall back to the cursor when all are taken, and among all-taken arms prefer one whose target is not a dead sink. Determinism and the no-random-seed property are kept.
close_reason: Arm choice is coverage-guided: an untaken arm first, then an arm from which some untaken branch edge is still reachable (backward frontier sweep), then the cursor. Measured on a 9181-node member: 336/6980 branches in 100 paths against 210/6980 for the round-robin, and path lengths went from half the run ending at 6 nodes to a 6-159 node spread. Sampling now also stops with 'nothing unexplored is reachable' when the entry cannot reach an untaken branch.

title: fields trace: an unparsed callee crashed the run instead of dead-ending
description: _called asked the loader for the callee before consulting the refusal, and _loaded read the cache file unconditionally, so a LINK to a member the parse never covered raised FileNotFoundError and ended a run of hundreds of paths. Any corpus selection LINKs outside itself, so this is the common case, not an edge one. Fix: _loaded is total -- an absent cache file returns Loaded(reason=callee-not-parsed: <path>), which _refusal ranks like every other reason, so the site becomes an opaque block that credits the commarea and lets the caller run on.
close_reason: _loaded is now total; trace reports the alias table's reason and the caller runs on

title: A write to a name with no memory definition is silently dropped
description:
A legacy corpus routinely refers to records whose copybook was never delivered. `operand_extents` already answers this without failing: no candidate cells yields `OperandExtents(reason="unknown-name")`, and on the SOURCE side `transfer._one_move` turns that into `Source(origin="UNKNOWN-NAME", extent=NOWHERE)` -- a dependency recorded against a zero-length extent that both `may_alias` and `must_cover` reject, so it can never alias real storage or kill a definition.

The TARGET side has no such path. All five write handlers iterate `operand_extents(operand, index).extents` directly (transfer.py:132, 165, 170, 217, 252), so an empty tuple yields zero `Write`s: `MOVE WS-A TO MISSING-REC` produces no flow, no definer, no dead-end note. The dependency does not become imprecise, it disappears. A consumer cannot distinguish "nothing was written here" from "the record this wrote to was never parsed".

`test_fixpoint.py:272` is named `test_every_resolvable_write_is_covered_in_a_program_with_no_unknown_names`, which is the suite conceding the gap rather than covering it.
design:
Emit one `Write` against a sentinel target when a target operand resolves to no extent, mirroring what the source side already does with NOWHERE. NOWHERE itself cannot be the target: `state.write` kills by `must_cover`, which a zero-length extent fails, so the write would be a weak update at a shared address and every unresolved target in the program would pile onto one key.

What is needed is one unaliasable target extent per unresolved NAME, so two missing records stay distinct and neither collides with real storage. Options: a distinct negative-start extent per name (the (-1,-1) shape), or a SPECIAL_REGISTERS sub-range keyed by name hash. Check first whether `FieldExtent` and the emitters tolerate a negative start -- `cobol_memory` is vendored and must not be modified.

Blast radius is the reason this is not folded into the path-sampling trace (red-dragon-forge-nxy): it changes `transfer.writes_of`, therefore the fixpoint, therefore all four artefact tables and every query resting on them. The trace reads `writes_of` and inherits whatever it returns, so it needs no change of its own and gains the fix for free.
acceptance_criteria: A synthetic program moving into a name that no record declares produces a flow whose target is the unresolved-name sentinel, distinct per name; the extents/defs artefacts carry it; `may_alias` and `must_cover` both reject it against every real extent in the program, so no definition is killed and no spurious edge is created; and the fixpoint suite gains a case that asserts this rather than excluding unknown names.

title: ASG drops every subject after the first in EVALUATE ... ALSO
description:
The parse records EVALUATE as a single 'subject' string and each WHEN as a single condition, so a multi-subject EVALUATE loses every dimension after the first. A two-subject EVALUATE with branches 'WHEN a ALSO x' / 'WHEN b ALSO x' / 'WHEN x ALSO a' collapses to 'WHEN a' / 'WHEN b' / 'WHEN x', and two branches that differed only in the dropped subject become indistinguishable duplicates. Consecutive WHENs sharing one body (a fall-through) are also flattened into separate branches each carrying a copy of that body, which changes the branch count even where the surviving literals differ.

Anything reading the ASG therefore reads a strictly weaker guard than the source states: a branch that fires only on a pair of values appears to fire on one of them alone. 104 members of the onboarded corpus contain a multi-subject EVALUATE, so this is not a corner case.

Detectable after the fact only by a tell -- two WHEN branches with an identical condition -- which catches the collapsed-duplicate shape and misses the rest.
design: Condition analysis over the ASG (extracting a program's top-level conditionals and formalising each aggregate condition) hit this on the first program examined. Fix shape: subject becomes a list, WHEN carries a list of choices aligned to it positionally (with ANY for the ALSO-ANY case), and consecutive subject-less WHENs keep their shared-body grouping rather than being duplicated.
acceptance_criteria: A multi-subject EVALUATE round-trips through the ASG with one entry per subject and per-branch choices aligned to them; a fall-through group of WHENs is represented once, not copied per WHEN.

title: cobble: extract BMS screen text the symbolic copybooks cannot carry
description:
hlasm_export already emits label, POS, INITIAL, ATTRB, PICIN/PICOUT and JUSTIFY for every DFHMDF, including the unnamed constant fields that hold the screen captions. bms_copybook_gen discards all of it: a symbolic map has no place for a caption (an unnamed DFHMDF produces no symbolic entry at all), so the generator is right to drop them and must keep doing so.

That leaves the screen text unreachable. Across one production corpus's 1032 maps the export carries 93588 DFHMDF invocations -- 54056 named, 39532 unnamed captions -- plus 14383 PICIN/PICOUT edit masks, and nothing reads them.

Add a cobble stage that runs the same hlasm_export the sym stage runs and serialises the full screen model as JSONL: one record per map, every field with label, pos, length, attrb, initial, picin, picout, justify, grpname, occurs and source line. Lossless -- pairing a caption to the field it labels is inference and belongs downstream, where the heuristic can be tuned without re-exporting.

Consumes the export JSON directly rather than bms_copybook_gen's model: that package carries 53 pre-existing fp-lint violations, so editing it blocks any commit that touches it, and changing its model risks perturbing byte-exact generated copybooks.

title: fields: a FLOWS_TO edge must state its byte-alignment rule instead of leaving it inferred
description: A consumer asking 'which bytes of the target did these source bytes land in' can only slice-map an edge when the move was byte-positional. Nothing on the edge says whether it was, so the only available test is len(source_extent) == len(target_extent) -- and that test is wrong. Measured over 25 members: 184 equal-length edges whose target strictly contains other declared fields, i.e. writes transfer.py did NOT fan out, i.e. _distributes was false (non-DISPLAY usage, CLAMPED target, or several source extents). Slice-mapping those is silently incorrect: a numeric or clamped move has no digit-to-byte correspondence to follow. The knowledge exists exactly where the write is built -- transfer._distributes already computes it -- and is unrecoverable downstream, so it has to be carried on the edge.
design: One attribute per edge naming the correspondence the move obeys: bytewise (source byte at relative offset k reached target relative offset k, so a sub-range slice-maps) versus whole (any source byte may have reached any target byte, so the only sound answer is the whole target extent). Set where _distributes is decided, threaded through Write/Source to FlowEdge, emitted in edge attrs. A synthetic origin has no source extent and so is whole by construction.
acceptance_criteria: Every FLOWS_TO edge carries the attribute. A distributed per-cell write is bytewise; a whole-group non-DISPLAY or CLAMPED write is whole; a synthetic-origin write is whole. Query-side slice-mapping keys off the attribute and never off extent lengths.
notes:
RESOLVED WITHOUT THE ATTRIBUTE. The premise -- that the correspondence rule is unrecoverable downstream -- no longer holds, because the normalisation published the two facts it needs.

An edge does not have to state the rule, because the rule is a function of things now on disk:
  - the target extent's clamp mark (trailing ~ in the wire form) says whether the target is EXACT;
  - extents.jsonl's usage column says whether either operand is a group or a non-DISPLAY elementary;
  - the two extents' lengths say whether the target was written whole or in part.

Whenever either operand is a group the MOVE is an alphanumeric byte copy: target byte k came from source byte k, and the tail past the source's end is spaces. A whole elementary target aligns on the decimal point instead, and a CLAMPED target has no correspondence at all. All three cases are decidable from the artefact.

fields.query.contributed() is that derivation, and is what makes the collapsed edge lossless -- the per-cell fan-out it replaces was 7842 of 9448 edges restating a fact the layout already fixes. Storing the rule per edge would have been the same duplication the normalisation removed.

Covered by tests/dataflow/fields/test_fields_query.py: the byte-offset case, a child past the source's end, a whole elementary target, and a clamped target.
close_reason: Premise refuted: the correspondence rule is derivable from the published usage column and the extent clamp mark, and is implemented as fields.query.contributed(). Carrying it per edge would restate what the declared layout already fixes.

title: FIELD nodes carry no extent, so coverage is only knowable where an edge names it
description:
Every FIELD node in the artefact has empty attrs -- no region, offset, or length. The geometry lives only on edges, as target_extent/source_extent strings, repeated once per edge.

Consequence: a consumer can CHECK containment between two extents that both appear on edges (same region, absolute start:end, interval arithmetic). They cannot ENUMERATE what a group write covers, because that needs the field layout and the artefact never publishes it. A child's extent enters the artefact only if some edge happens to name that child.

Two mechanisms currently patch over this, both writing the same information repeatedly:
 - fan-out in _initialize_writes and _distributed (dataflow/fields/transfer.py:209, 129), which emits one row per elementary cell
 - --expand's target_fields/source_fields, one covering-field list per edge

Putting region/start/end on the FIELD node makes enumeration derivable and collapses both: INITIALIZE's fan-out becomes redundant (all its cells share one synthetic LITERAL source), target_fields becomes derivable so --expand can go, and the per-edge extent strings become recoverable from endpoint plus node.

One fan-out stays load-bearing. _distributed's per-cell writes each carry a different source slice, and cells past the end of the source get LITERAL_SPACES (_cell_write, line 109). That is a distribution rule, not containment, and is not recoverable from the group-level pair alone.

Related: there is no query layer over this artefact at all -- cobble-fields is build-only, and nothing in the tree reads edges.jsonl. Whatever consumer arrives first will need enumeration, so the node geometry should land before it does.
design:
DECIDED: geometry on FIELD node attrs (region, start, end, level, optionally parent). Consumers resolve coverage by interval overlap.

Rejected: a CONTAINS edge kind. It encodes the declared level tree, but COBOL storage is overlapping views -- a write to a field changes the children of a REDEFINES view of it, which are not under it in the tree, so a traversal returns a partial answer that looks complete. Consumers would need interval arithmetic anyway, plus a second answer to reconcile. Node extents are the primitive from which both the tree and the overlaps derive; CONTAINS can be layered on later, the reverse is not recoverable.

Scope that follows:
 - add region/start/end/level(/parent) to FIELD node attrs in dataflow/fields/emit.py
 - retire --expand and the target_fields/source_fields columns (69% of the artefact); covering_fields becomes a query, not an emitted column
 - retire the synthetic-origin fan-out in _initialize_writes and _origin_writes (29% of rows); one group write row, consumer enumerates
 - KEEP _distributed's per-cell writes: each carries a different source slice with LITERAL_SPACES past the source end, a distribution rule that is not recoverable from the group-level pair
acceptance_criteria: A FIELD node states its region and byte range. A consumer can enumerate the fields a group write covers using nodes.jsonl and edges.jsonl alone, with no CellIndex and no --expand.
notes:
DELIVERED, with two departures from the DESIGN above.

1. Geometry did NOT go on FIELD node attrs. It is its own file, extents.jsonl, one row per declared name: {id, level, usage, extents[]}. nodes.jsonl now carries nothing but ids. Where a field IS is true whether or not a value ever moved through it, so it is not a graph fact; and the layout of a member is several times the size of its flows. 'Declared' is the load-bearing word -- an edge names only the smallest field covering the bytes it moved, so the children a group write filled are absent from the graph and present here.

level is published because a group with one child and a REDEFINES pair own identical bytes: 14165 of 47741 ranges are owned by more than one declared name, and only the level says which contains which. usage because a partial overlap of a COMP/COMP-3 field is not a partial read of its value.

2. The last paragraph is refuted: _distributed's fan-out was NOT load-bearing and is gone. A group move is now one edge naming the group, and which source bytes each child received is derived by fields.query.contributed() from the two extents plus the declared layout -- byte k from byte k when either operand is a group, NO_RANGE for a child past the source's end (the spaces case the fan-out encoded). 7842 of 9448 real-source edges were per-cell rows restating that. The group-move _is_display guard went with it.

Also delivered, beyond this bead: defs.jsonl. 862 of 5261 (node, source extent, target extent) triples have more than one reaching definer, one has 100; pinned to the edge they were duplicated per path and then deduplicated by endpoint, keeping one nondeterministically. source_node is off the edge.

The query layer this bead flagged as missing now exists: cobble-fields-query, seven queries over the four tables, every predicate intersecting byte ranges rather than matching ids. That distinction is not cosmetic -- measured on one corpus field, an id join returns zero writers and zero readers where the byte query returns the one real writer, because the only write is a file READ INTO the enclosing 2000-byte record.
close_reason: Delivered as four normalised tables (nodes/edges/extents/defs) plus a byte-interval query surface, rather than as node attrs; the per-cell fan-out the bead thought load-bearing is derivable and gone.

title: GraphWriter edge dedup collapses distinct dataflow facts, nondeterministically
description: graph_writer.add_edge keys dedup on (source, source_kind, target, target_kind, kind) and drops any later edge with the same key, ignoring attrs entirely. In the fields stage attrs carry the writing node, the source byte extent and the target byte extent, so N distinct byte-level flows between the same field pair collapse to one row. Measured on one member: a STRING with two ref-mod sendings of one field produced 6 FlowEdges (2 extents x 3 defining nodes) and 1 emitted row; a 1-byte field had 4 inbound and 4 outbound FlowEdges and emitted 2 and 1. Which row survives is order-dependent, and Write.sources is a frozenset, so iteration order varies with the per-process hash seed: two runs of the SAME walk over the SAME input differ. Reproduced with two --sweeps 1 runs differing in 2 edges.
design: Not a fields-stage bug in origin -- the dedup is shared infrastructure and other stages may rely on endpoint-level collapse. Options: include attrs in the key, or give the fields stage a writer that does. Either way the nondeterminism has to go: a stage whose output changes between identical runs cannot be diffed across a corpus, which is how regressions in this pipeline get caught. Note the analysis itself is correct and complete; only the emitted artefact loses facts.
acceptance_criteria: Two runs of the same walk over the same member produce byte-identical edges.jsonl, and distinct (writing node, source extent) flows between one field pair each get a row.
close_reason: Edge identity is now per-kind (ATTRS_ARE_IDENTITY names FLOWS_TO), emit carries source_node, and the walk sorts each statement's edges so output no longer depends on the hash seed. Verified: identical output across seven PYTHONHASHSEED values; two flows between one field pair differing only in defining node both emit.

title: Fields emit drops the defining node from every edge
description: fixpoint computes Source as (origin, extent, node), where node is where the value was last defined -- the whole point of settling the state before extraction. emit._attrs writes node (the WRITING statement), source_extent and target_extent, but never source.node. So edges.jsonl cannot answer which statement defined the value that flowed, only which statement moved it. Observed: a 1-byte field had 4 inbound FlowEdges whose defining nodes were two group INITIALIZEs and two EXEC CICS READ INTO statements; the file shows none of the four, because the column does not exist.
design: This is why a group-level file read looks absent from a child field: the covering group write IS resolved by must_cover and IS credited as the source, but the defining node is discarded on the way out. Fix is an attrs key (source_node), not a change to the walk. Blocked-by relationship with the dedup bug: adding the column changes nothing while GraphWriter collapses rows on endpoints alone.
acceptance_criteria: An edge whose source was defined by a group write names the defining statement in attrs.
close_reason: Edge identity is now per-kind (ATTRS_ARE_IDENTITY names FLOWS_TO), emit carries source_node, and the walk sorts each statement's edges so output no longer depends on the hash seed. Verified: identical output across seven PYTHONHASHSEED values; two flows between one field pair differing only in defining node both emit.

title: Widen the per-extent source set to bound fixpoint height
description:
fixpoint.py's docstring argues termination from 'every extent a transfer can construct is fixed by the statement set before iteration begins'. That part is true -- extent.py folds only literals, and any non-constant subscript or reference modification collapses to CLAMPED over the whole base extent, so the key set is finite and fixed.

What the argument undercounts is height. State maps an extent to a SET of defining nodes, and adding one source to one extent enlarges the successor's state and re-enqueues it. The growth-event bound is therefore O(extents x nodes), not O(1) per node. Measured: a 3919-node member saturated reach at 3911/3919 and was still not converged after 195,950 dequeues (ITERATION_FACTOR 50).

Reach is not the problem -- 99.8% of nodes were reached. The unconverged part is provenance precision: which definitions reach each use.

Widening: once one extent accumulates more than k defining nodes, collapse the set to a marker meaning 'many'. Height becomes extents x k, reach is unaffected, and the only thing lost is the full enumeration of definitions for the handful of extents that have more than k -- which is not a fact anyone reads off an edge anyway.
design:
State is Mapping[FieldExtent, frozenset[Source]] and a Source is a TRIPLE (origin, extent, node), so the set under one extent holds one entry per distinct (upstream value, writing node) pair -- not one per writing node. join (state.py:60) unions those sets per key, and _grown (fixpoint.py:157) re-enqueues a successor whenever its entry state enlarges. The growth-event bound is therefore nodes x extents x |distinct sources|, not nodes x extents. The extent KEY set is finite and fixed before iteration (extent.py:317-331 narrows only when precision is EXACT and both start and length constant-fold, else collapses to CLAMPED over the whole base) -- so the height lives entirely in the per-key source sets.

The measurement agrees: on a 3919-node member, queued sat at ~3250 for tens of thousands of dequeues while reach was already 3911/3919. Reach was finished; the walk was grinding source-set unions.

Widening caps that dimension. Choose k; when a key's set would exceed k, replace it with WIDE, an absorbing element (join(WIDE, anything) = WIDE, so once widened always widened, and monotonicity holds). Each key's chain is then at most k+1 steps, giving nodes x extents x (k+1) with k chosen rather than inherited from the corpus. It touches exactly two functions -- join and write in state.py -- because those are the only places a set grows.

Cost, stated honestly: widening changes the ANSWER, not just the schedule. For an extent with more than k sources the enumeration is gone. Raising --iteration-factor is the only option that keeps provenance exact; one-pass (red-dragon-forge-hbe) drops loop-carried flow instead but is sound as an under-approximation and far cheaper. Prefer widening when the loop-carried answer is needed under a bound.

The marker must reach the emitted edge -- reaching() returns it and emit flags the edge -- so a widened claim is never presented as an exact one. That is the red-dragon-forge-9fa failure mode.

Decide k by measurement, not guess: what fraction of a real member's extents exceed k for k in 4, 8, 16. A handful means widening is nearly free; most of them means the marker becomes the answer everywhere and this is the wrong fix.
acceptance_criteria: A synthetic program with more than k definitions of one extent converges and marks the widened edges; the 3919-node member converges under the default factor; reach stays at its pre-widening value.

title: A field-dataflow fixpoint that hits its dequeue cap reports coverage as if it converged
description:
During the Task 7 acceptance run one member logged 'fields: dequeue cap 74950 reached ... (1499 nodes)'. The fixpoint stops at that cap and returns, and the ProgramFlow it returns carries writes/covered counters that the corpus pass then folds into the coverage ratio as though the analysis had converged. It had not, so that member's coverage number is not trustworthy and the run still exits 0.

This is the 3ao failure mode arriving from a different direction: 3ao was a walk that reached 18% of nodes while its suite passed because nothing measured reach. Here reach IS measured, but a capped run is counted as a complete one.
design: ProgramFlow should carry the fact that it was capped -- a field alongside skipped, or a reason value -- so build_corpus can report capped members separately and decide whether a capped member belongs in the coverage denominator at all. A capped member counted as covered inflates the ratio; excluded, it at least does not lie. Either is better than silence. The corpus pass's exit status should say something about it too; today it cannot.
acceptance_criteria: A member whose fixpoint hits the cap is named in the run report, and the JSON summary carries a capped count. A test builds a program that trips the cap and asserts both.

title: forge has no beads redactor, so issues/issues.jsonl cannot be regenerated
description: CLAUDE.md mandates 'bd export -o issues/issues.jsonl && git add issues/issues.jsonl' before committing anything that touches issues, but forge has no redactor (red-dragon has scripts/redact-beads-issues). Several issues in the local Dolt DB carry corpus identifiers in their titles and bodies -- red-dragon-forge-3ao names one in its title -- so a plain export writes them into a tracked file, which the no-external-identifiers rule forbids. Effect: the tracked snapshot is frozen. Every bead closed or created since it last diverged (opi, zkk, z9h, j7w, and aj3's rescope) exists only in the local DB, so a fresh clone rebuilds an out-of-date graph and no other machine sees the work.
design: Port red-dragon's scripts/redact-beads-issues, or make export refuse when a redaction pass would change any field. Redaction has to be idempotent and stable: a field that reduces to a different placeholder on each run makes issues/issues.jsonl churn on every export and the diffs unreviewable.
acceptance_criteria: bd export -o issues/issues.jsonl produces a file containing no corpus identifiers, running it twice produces byte-identical output, and the CLAUDE.md workflow step is executable as written.

title: Rebuild the ASG cache and gate on what its operands carry
description: The current cache predates both the bridge jar that emits structured subscripts and the upstream extent work, so its MOVE operands are bare names. Bead 8y0 was filed as a P0 bridge defect on that evidence and retracted once the cache turned out to be the cause. Nothing downstream can tell a stale cache from a corpus property by reading it, so this adds a diagnostic that counts MOVE operand shapes (bare / subscripted / reference-modified) and exits non-zero on a cache with no subscripts, then re-parses into a fresh asg_dir and validates it. Precondition for any field-level extent work.
design: Parse is skip-if-cached and the existing cache is 557 MB and roughly four hours of JVM, so the re-parse writes to a fresh asg_dir rather than clobbering the cache the srccfg work reads. Diagnostic lands as cobble.diagnosis.asg_operands with a diagnose-asg-operands entry point, following the layout_check precedent of a committed cross-check rather than a throwaway script.
acceptance_criteria: diagnose-asg-operands exits 0 with a non-zero subscripted count on the new cache and 1 on the old one; new cache program count at or above the old; fail count not risen.
close_reason: Done: corpus re-parsed into a fresh cache and gated by diagnose-asg-operands. 102,922 subscripted MOVE operands where the old cache had 0; total (1,452,562) and ref_modified (11,252) byte-identical, so the re-parse changed what operands carry, not which statements exist. 3,779 JSON / 0 .fail.

title: Extract the COBOL byte-extent algebra to a static-surface package
description: The alias algebra (FieldExtent/Precision/RegionId/AbstractLocation/StorageIdentifier, ~190 lines) sits under interpreter/, which the cobble-no-interpreter contract forbids cobble from importing. It has no IR dependency, so it moves upstream to a new sibling package cobol_memory, mirroring cobol_asg. Cobble then runs its own fixpoint over its own CFG keyed on FieldExtent, and the interpreter's fixpoint driver stays put. Upstream change: lands in red-dragon, arrives here as a submodule bump.
design: Sibling package, not a subpackage: an import of interpreter.anything runs interpreter/__init__.py and loads the VM. Needs a root_packages entry, a cobol-memory-is-a-leaf forbidden contract, and pyproject packages list. Runtime test asserts interpreter is absent from sys.modules after importing cobol_memory.
acceptance_criteria: cobol_memory importable without loading interpreter; lint-imports clean in both repos; red-dragon suite green; forge cobble suite green.
close_reason: Done: cobol_memory shipped as a sibling package in red-dragon (extent/precision/region), reached from cobble via the submodule bump. Guarded by a subprocess test asserting 'interpreter' never enters sys.modules, since import-linter cannot see that an import triggers VM loading.

title: srccfg CFG flattens group/member names, breaking dataflow at the record-area boundary
description:
The source CFG treats an 01 record area and its subordinate fields as unrelated names, so a dataflow chain snaps wherever COBOL relies on group containment. Verified on PROG-UPD (bundle: the srccfg bundle for PROG-UPD).

The write path for MST-APP-COUNT, from source the online source for PROG-UPD (path in the untracked corpus notes):
  3652  PERFORM UPD-MASTER THRU UPD-MASTER-EXIT
  4149    PERFORM READ-UPD-MST  -> 4863 EXEC CICS READ FILE('FILE-MST') INTO(MST-REC) RIDFLD(MST-REGION-KEY) UPDATE
  4275    MOVE SCR-APP-COUNT TO MST-APP-COUNT   (one of ~130 field overlays)
  4355    PERFORM REWRITE-MST   -> 5191 EXEC CICS REWRITE FILE('FILE-MST') FROM(MST-REC)

The CFG models the VSAM handoff itself correctly: READ-UPD-MST/3 is CICS_READ writes MST-REC reads FILE:FILE-MST; REWRITE-MST/0 is CICS_REWRITE writes FILE:FILE-MST reads MST-REC; the PERFORM and THRU-fallthrough edges are all present and statement indices line up with the source.

What is missing is the join. The CFG's name universe for PROG-UPD has 1064 distinct names: MST-REC, FILE:FILE-MST, and 134 separate MST-* fields, with nothing relating them. Consequences, both reproduced:

1. Forward/backward chains do not cross the boundary. `cobble-srccfg derivation FILE:FILE-MST` prints one line, 'FILE:FILE-MST <- external identifier (FILE)'. The graph cannot answer 'does this field reach VSAM', which is the question a reader of a CICS update program actually has.
2. A group write does not kill its members. READ-UPD-MST/0 (MOVE SPACES TO MST-REC) and /1 (INITIALIZE MST-REC) wipe all 134 MST-* fields, yet `writers MST-APP-COUNT` reports exactly one writer. The killing write is invisible.

The hierarchy is not missing from the input -- srccfg discards it. The ASG in the parse cache for PROG-UPD carries data_fields as a nested tree with level/pic/offset per node: '01 MST-REC / 05 MST-APP-COUNT', and '01 COMM-AREA / 05 CASE-INFO / 10 SCR-APP-COUNT'. So this is a projection the CFG builder drops, not analysis that has to be invented.

Distinct from red-dragon-forge-3ao, which is the reaching walk finding no path to these same nodes. Both bite this write path at once: UPD-MASTER/57 and REWRITE-MST/0 each print 'unreachable from PROG-UPD entry' today.
acceptance_criteria: 1. MST-APP-COUNT and MST-REC are related in the CFG, by whatever seam is chosen (containment edges, or a name-to-ancestors map carried on the Cfg). 2. A write to a group is reported as affecting its members, so `writers MST-APP-COUNT` names the INITIALIZE/MOVE SPACES at READ-UPD-MST/0-1. 3. A backward chain from FILE:FILE-MST reaches MST-APP-COUNT and then SCR-APP-COUNT. 4. Tests pin both directions on a small fixture with a nested 01/05/10 record.
notes:
Open design question: whether REDEFINES and offset-overlap aliasing come in with the same change or are deferred. data_fields already carries offset, so the information is there; scope it deliberately rather than by accident.
Redacted 2026-09-07: corpus program, file, field and paragraph names replaced with stable pseudonyms (PROG-*, FILE-*, MST-*, SCR-*, BUF-*, LAY-*, MSG-*). Measured numbers and source line references are unchanged. The mapping and the pre-redaction text are in .knowledge_graph_scratch/ (untracked, per-machine).
close_reason: Subsumed by the byte-extent model: containment, REDEFINES, OCCURS and reference modification all fall out of extent overlap. See the field-level byte dataflow spec.

title: srccfg reaching_conditions finds no path to 82% of PROG-UPD
description:
On PROG-UPD (3919 nodes, 12-program closure in the srccfg bundle for PROG-UPD), reaching_conditions() returns zero guards for 3224 of 3919 nodes. query.py then renders those as 'unreachable from PROG-UPD entry', which is a positive claim the walk did not establish.

Concrete case: UPD-MASTER/57 (MOVE SCR-APP-COUNT TO MST-APP-COUNT, source line 4275). Raw edge BFS from MAIN-PROC#label reaches 3911/3919 nodes including this one; the paragraph is entered by PROC-UPDATE/8 --PERFORM--> UPD-MASTER#label (source line 3652: PERFORM UPD-MASTER THRU UPD-MASTER-EXIT) and by PRIOR-EXIT#end --FALLTHRU-->.

Ruled out: not the MAX_PATHS cap (paths=0 at max_paths 64, 256 and 1024); not \`abandoned\` (node absent from reaching.abandoned, so the \"route not found by walk\" wording never fires); not \`overflowed\`. The unreached set is whole paragraphs (STARTBR-FILE-C, READNEXT-FILE-C, READ-FILE-D, READ-FILE-E, READ-FILE-B, GET-NEW-ITEM, ... plus every #label/#end/#exit), which points at PERFORM THRU / fallthrough handling in the walk rather than at any one statement.

Effect: guards and derivation reports are unusable on this member, and misleadingly confident. writers and coassign are unaffected (they are structural).

Two things to fix: the walk, and the wording -- a node with zero guards that raw edge reachability CAN reach must not be printed as unreachable.
acceptance_criteria: 1. UPD-MASTER/57 gets a non-empty guard list, or is reported with wording that does not claim unreachability. 2. The no-guard node count for PROG-UPD is a small fraction, consistent with raw edge reachability (3911/3919). 3. A regression test pins a PERFORM ... THRU target paragraph as guard-reachable.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE (measured, synthetic COBOL only -- no corpus identifiers).

A CALL node keeps a FLOW edge to the next statement AND a PERFORM edge into the paragraph, and the paragraph's RETURN lands on that same FLOW target. Walking both double-counts every path, so _not_a_second_route_past_a_call refuses the FLOW edge while it predicts the RETURN will fire. _return_pending makes that prediction at GRAPH level ('does a RETURN edge exist whose source has any predecessor'); the blockage is at PATH level. When the range end is unreachable on this path, the RETURN never fires, nothing revisits the refusal, and the walk dies at the call. Everything after it is zero-guard -- and since a driver paragraph performs everything, that is the program.

TRIGGER, isolated to one shape: a paragraph performed on its own that lies STRICTLY INSIDE a later PERFORM ... THRU range. NOT the range start, NOT the range end (already in seen, so the prediction correctly reports 'spent'), NOT a paragraph outside the range. A nested PERFORM / overlapping range is NOT required -- the earlier 'PERFORM THRU linking is broken' framing was too narrow.

BLAST RADIUS: 59% / 83% / 94% of nodes zeroed as the driver grew from 2 to 40 performs. Scales with the driver's length, consistent with the 82% reported here. truncated and overflowed were 0 throughout, so the cap is genuinely uninvolved -- consistent with the max_paths 64/256/1024 experiment.

THIS BEAD'S 'ruled out: node absent from abandoned' REASONING WAS INVALID. abandoned was a one-step boundary predicate and was NOT closed forward, so absence only meant 'not at the boundary'. Measured 43 of 45 zero-guard nodes absent from it.

FIX (dataflow.py):
1. _resumed_where_a_return_never_came -- after the walk, any node with a PERFORM edge that HAS arrivals whose FLOW continuation has NONE is a call the walk went into and never came back from. Re-seed the continuation with that call's own arrivals and sweep again, to a fixpoint. Sound rather than approximate: a PERFORM returns to the next statement under the guard that reached it, and FLOW out of a CALL is a return point, not a fallthrough. Terminates because a round only seeds nodes with no arrivals and every seeded node is recorded.
2. _Arrival value object; _Sweep records (guard, stack) per node instead of guards alone. The stack is load-bearing and its absence was a real defect in the first cut of the fix: resuming with no frames makes a paragraph end take the FALLTHRU to the next paragraph and REFUSE the RETURN to its caller -- exactly backwards. Measured: it invented an unconditional guard for a paragraph nothing performs.
3. _recorded dedupes arrivals by (guard, stack). Without it a continuation is recorded twice -- once from the seed, once from the RETURN that finally fires after the resume -- reintroducing the double-count the FLOW rule exists to prevent.
4. _abandoned closed forward through unguarded nodes only (stopping at guarded ones: their successors were walked, so their emptiness is a different claim). This is the second fix the bead asked for -- query.py:88's 'unreachable from <program> entry' is now printed only for nodes with no guarded node leading to them at all. No wording change was needed once the set was right.

RESULT: blast-radius probe 94% -> 1%. The residual 3 nodes are the genuinely-unwalked range end, no longer scaling with program size, and every zero-guard node is now named abandoned (0 falsely reported unreachable).

TESTS (tests/dataflow/srccfg/test_reaching.py): added test_a_call_whose_return_never_fires_does_not_zero_the_rest_of_the_program (the trigger shape) and test_resuming_past_a_stranded_call_returns_from_its_frame_and_does_not_fall_through (the stack, via a paragraph nothing performs). Rewrote test_a_node_the_walk_gave_up_on_is_named_abandoned_rather_than_dead, which had pinned the loss as correct-by-design; it now asserts every node of the unwalked paragraph is named and that the loss stops at the call. Full cobble suite green, Black clean, pyright 0.

FOLLOW-UP FILED: red-dragon-forge-a3d -- abandoned now over-reports where a FALLTHRU was correctly refused as never-executing. Safe direction, P3, deliberately not folded in.

NOT VERIFIED against the real member: the acceptance suite skips without cobble/config/srccfg-tests.toml.

title: CALL USING marshals every argument out of WORKING-STORAGE, whatever section it is declared in
description:
interpreter/cobol/lower_call.py:47 binds ws_reg from materialised.working_storage and line 60 does 'fl, _ = materialised.resolve(param.name)', DISCARDING the owning region that resolve returns. Copy-in and copy-back then both use ws_reg unconditionally.

So a CALL USING argument declared in LINKAGE or LOCAL-STORAGE is marshalled from the WORKING-STORAGE region at the field's offset-within-its-own-section. The callee receives whatever bytes happen to sit at that offset in WS.

VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY (not by inspection). Probe: WS = [WS-ALPHA X(10), WS-BETA X(8)], LINKAGE = [LK-FOO X(8)]. resolve('LK-FOO') returns offset 0, length 8, owning region %1 (LINKAGE). The emitted LoadRegion reads region %0 (WORKING-STORAGE) at offset 0 length 8 — i.e. the first 8 bytes of WS-ALPHA. Repeating with LOCAL-STORAGE [LS-BAR X(4)]: owning region %2, CALL reads %0. Both sections affected; resolve's precedence is LOCAL-STORAGE > WORKING-STORAGE > LINKAGE, so any argument not in WS is wrong.

WORSE ON BY REFERENCE: the copy-back WriteRegion also targets ws_reg at the same offset, so the callee's output is written ON TOP of the unrelated WS field. It is not only a bad read — it silently corrupts WORKING-STORAGE on return.

Why it survived: the false invariant is asserted in the code rather than checked. lower_call.py:51 says '# Resolve field layouts for all USING params (all are in WS).' and the docstring repeats 'Copy each USING field from WS'. MaterialisedSectionedLayout.resolve was later given a region return value and this caller was never updated.

REACHABILITY: passing a LINKAGE item to a further CALL is the standard 'hand my caller's parameter down' pattern and is common in production COBOL.

SIBLING, SAME FAMILY: statement_dispatch.py:100 passes only the WS (layout, region) pair to lower_move_corresponding, with the comment 'uses first WS section' — so MOVE CORRESPONDING on a LINKAGE or LOCAL-STORAGE group has the same defect. Filed here because the fix is the same shape.

NOT a bug, checked: lower_search.py:48 discards the region but only reads fl.occurs_count. lower_arithmetic.py:641 _find_group_and_reg iterates the sections and returns the matching (layout, reg) pair — that is the correct existing pattern to model the fix on.
acceptance_criteria: A CALL USING an argument declared in LINKAGE marshals from the LINKAGE region, and a BY REFERENCE copy-back writes to the LINKAGE region — asserted on emitted IR and on an executed program whose callee mutates the argument. Same for LOCAL-STORAGE. MOVE CORRESPONDING on a non-WS group resolves against its own section.
notes:
CORRECTION to the sibling claim in the description. I wrote that MOVE CORRESPONDING 'has the same defect'. It does not — verified by probe: MOVE CORRESPONDING from a LINKAGE group raises loudly,

  KeyError: "Group not found in layout: 'LK-REC'"

because lower_move_corresponding (lower_arithmetic.py:610) receives one DataLayout and one Register for BOTH operands, and lookup_group on the WS layout misses. So it is a LOUD unsupported-case, not silent corruption — a materially lower severity than the CALL bug, and it should not be conflated with it.

The real MOVE CORRESPONDING limitation is structural: a single (layout, region) pair cannot express operands in two different sections, and MOVE CORRESPONDING LK-REC TO WS-REC is the common shape. Fixing it means giving it a per-operand region, the way _find_group_and_reg (lower_arithmetic.py:634) already resolves them.

The CALL USING bug in the description stands as verified.
close_reason:
Fixed in red-dragon e1e8875d, vendored here as a1af3a1f.

lower_call now takes the owning region from materialised.resolve per parameter, for both copy-in and BY REFERENCE copy-back. Per option 2 of the brainstorm it also stops binding a whole-section register while marshalling at all — the WS region is bound only at the one line that legitimately needs it (restoring the caller's __ws_region after the call) — so there is no section-wide register in scope to reach for by mistake.

Proven at runtime, not just on IR: a new integration test chains CHAINA -> CHAINB -> CHAINC, where CHAINB hands its LINKAGE item down. Before the fix CHAINC received 9999 (CHAINB's WS-DECOY) instead of 5. A unit test locks both LINKAGE and LOCAL-STORAGE at the IR level and was mutation-checked — reverting the fix turns it red.

red-dragon suite: 15065 passed, 66 skipped, 17 xfailed, no regressions. cicada 449 passed, forge 62 passed against the bump.

NOT fixed here, deliberately: the MOVE CORRESPONDING limitation recorded in the notes. It raises loudly rather than corrupting, so it is a different severity and belongs in its own change — lower_move_corresponding takes a single (layout, region) pair and cannot express operands in two sections.

title: CICS prepass injects copybooks into the main source only, so CALLed subprograms using HANDLE CONDITION cannot compile
description:
build_cics_spec's source_prepass is folded over the MAIN source only (interpreter.project.coprocessor_compile.compile_program), so DFHEIBLK and DFHHANDLE are never injected into a disk-resolved CALL callee or an extra_subprogram_sources module. A subprogram containing EXEC CICS HANDLE CONDITION therefore fails to compile unless it carries its own COPY DFHHANDLE by hand.

Found while adding the multi-module isolation test in Task 5 of the condition-handling plan (commit 4c58a1e5): cicada/tests/integration/cics/test_condition_handling.py's HNDLINKB fixture works around this with an explicit COPY DFHHANDLE, which real corpus subprograms will not have.

Same gap applies to EIBRESP references (DFHEIBLK) in any CALLed subprogram, so it is broader than condition handling.
acceptance_criteria: A CALLed subprogram containing EXEC CICS HANDLE CONDITION, with no hand-written COPY DFHHANDLE, compiles and numbers its own handlers. The HNDLINKB fixture's explicit COPY DFHHANDLE can be removed and its test still passes.
notes: Confirmed live in Task 6 (commit 396bf478): a callee needs BOTH copybooks, not just DFHHANDLE. COPY DFHHANDLE. supplies DFH-HANDLER/DFH-RAISABLE; COPY DFHEIBLK. supplies EIBRESP. The Task 5 HNDLINKB fixture had only the former and tripped the new guard, which is the guard working as intended. CicsLoweringStrategy._emit_dispatcher_if_needed now raises NotImplementedError naming this bead when a module registers handlers but lacks either field.
