title: COBOL: PERFORM VARYING with FROM LENGTH OF + reference-modified loop-variable subscript in UNTIL loops incorrectly
description:
PERFORM VARYING WS-IDX FROM LENGTH OF WS-S BY -1 UNTIL WS-S(WS-IDX:1) NOT = SPACES OR WS-IDX = 1 terminates with the wrong index. Verified: WS-S PIC X(4) VALUE 'AB  ' -> final WS-IDX = 0 (expected 2, the position of the last non-space char). 

NOTE: base PERFORM VARYING works, INCLUDING descending (PERFORM VARYING I FROM 5 BY -1 UNTIL I < 1 correctly iterates 5 times). The gap is this combination: (a) FROM LENGTH OF <field> as the initial value, and/or (b) a reference-modified subscript that uses the loop variable — WS-S(WS-IDX:1) — re-evaluated against the changing WS-IDX in the UNTIL condition. The construct lowers without error but loops wrong. Implementer should isolate which of (a)/(b) is at fault (likely the ref-mod-subscript-in-condition re-evaluation, possibly the LENGTH OF FROM init).

Surfaced in COMEN01C PROCESS-ENTER-KEY: it scans the entered OPTION field right-to-left to find its significant length before parsing the option number.
acceptance_criteria: PERFORM VARYING WS-IDX FROM LENGTH OF WS-S BY -1 UNTIL WS-S(WS-IDX:1) NOT = SPACES OR WS-IDX = 1 leaves WS-IDX at the last non-space position (2 for 'AB  '); FROM LENGTH OF and ref-mod-subscript-in-UNTIL both evaluate correctly each iteration.
notes: Re-spike after 0cci: the real COMEN01C menu-action happy path works (option 01 parsed correctly -> WS-OPTION=1 -> XCTL COACTVWC), so the option-length scan yields the right result for clean input in the real flow. The isolation failure (final idx 0 for 'AB  ') may not replicate the exact real construct or is masked for well-formed input. Keep open (real isolation gap) but NOT a happy-path blocker -> P2; revisit if a malformed/odd option exposes it.
close_reason: PERFORM VARYING FROM <expr> (LENGTH OF) now evaluated as an expression instead of stored as a literal string; ref-mod operands (WS-S(WS-IDX:1)) in a condition relation decode+slice per iteration. Structured (bridge emits {kind:length_of}/ref_mod fields), no regex, no core. Full suite 14050 green.

title: COBOL: class conditions (IS [NOT] NUMERIC / ALPHABETIC / ...) not lowered
description:
Class conditions are not lowered: IF WS-X IS NUMERIC always takes the ELSE branch. Verified: WS-X PIC X(2) VALUE '01'; IF WS-X IS NUMERIC MOVE 1 ELSE MOVE 2 -> result is 2 (ELSE), should be 1. condition_lowering.py has no class-condition handling (grep for NUMERIC/ALPHABETIC/class -> none); it falls through to the text/never-match path. (z31u deferred CLASS/SIGN conditions.)

Scope (language feature): lower the COBOL class conditions IS [NOT] NUMERIC, ALPHABETIC, ALPHABETIC-LOWER, ALPHABETIC-UPPER (and user-defined class names if present). The bridge already serializes a structured class node (z31u contract: {t:class, not, operand, class:NUMERIC|...}); the frontend condition lowering must emit the actual test:
  - NUMERIC: every byte of the field is a digit (per its category/PIC; for DISPLAY numeric, all 0-9, sign handling for signed).
  - ALPHABETIC: every byte A-Z/a-z/space; ALPHABETIC-LOWER/UPPER accordingly.
Surfaced in COMEN01C menu: 'IF WS-OPTION IS NOT NUMERIC OR WS-OPTION > CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT ...' validates the entered option; without NUMERIC the validation is wrong. The '> count' relation already works.
acceptance_criteria: IF X IS NUMERIC true for all-digit X, false otherwise; IS NOT NUMERIC inverts; ALPHABETIC variants work; integrated into the structured condition lowering (no silent never-match).
notes: Re-spike after 0cci: the real COMEN01C menu-action HAPPY PATH works (valid option 01 -> XCTL COACTVWC) WITHOUT this fix. Reason: COMEN01C's check is 'IF WS-OPTION IS NOT NUMERIC OR > count OR = 0'; for a VALID numeric option all disjuncts are false whether or not NUMERIC is correctly lowered, so the broken class condition produces the same (false) result. This bug only manifests on INVALID input (non-numeric option should be rejected but isn't). Real but edge-path, not a flow blocker -> P2.
close_reason: Class conditions IS [NOT] NUMERIC/ALPHABETIC now lower from a structured {not,class,operand} node (bridge) to a CallFunction against COBOL-layer builtins (__is_numeric/__is_alphabetic). No text re-parse, no core. Full suite 14047 green.

title: COBOL: figurative VALUE (VALUE SPACES/ZEROS/LOW-VALUES) stored as literal text, not the figurative fill
description:
A data item declared with a figurative VALUE clause stores the literal NAME instead of the figurative fill. E.g. '01 WS-X PIC X(4) VALUE SPACES.' initializes WS-X to the text 'SPAC' (the word 'SPACES' encoded + truncated) rather than 4 actual spaces; likewise VALUE ZEROS / LOW-VALUES / HIGH-VALUES / QUOTES. Surfaced while fixing condition lowering (red-dragon-z31u): integration tests had to use 'MOVE SPACES TO WS-X' to initialize fields because 'VALUE SPACES' produced wrong bytes, isolating it as a separate data-division-init defect.

Root area: the VALUE-clause encoding path in the COBOL frontend (interpreter/cobol/lower_data_division.py -> ctx.emit_field_encode(region_reg, fl, fl.value) -> emit_encode_value in interpreter/cobol/emit_context.py -> encode_alphanumeric). This is the SAME init path that red-dragon-3mx4 fixed for hex literals (X'nn'): emit_encode_value got a special case for hex literals (parse_hex_literal) but NOT for figurative constants. A figurative VALUE arrives as fl.value == 'SPACES' (a bare name) and is encoded as character data.

Fix: detect figurative constants in the VALUE-encoding path and fill the field accordingly, sized to the field's byte length and respecting category:
  SPACE/SPACES   -> all spaces (EBCDIC 0x40 across the field)
  ZERO/ZEROS/ZEROES -> all zeros (numeric 0 / EBCDIC '0' 0xF0 per field category)
  LOW-VALUE/LOW-VALUES   -> 0x00 bytes
  HIGH-VALUE/HIGH-VALUES -> 0xFF bytes
  QUOTE/QUOTES   -> quote char
Confirm whether ProLeap/the bridge surfaces a figurative VALUE distinctly (a figurative marker) or as the bare name 'SPACES' in fl.value; prefer detecting it structurally if the bridge exposes it, else recognize the canonical figurative names. Note: a real field literally named the same as a figurative is not valid COBOL, so name-matching is safe, but structural detection is cleaner.

Not on the sign-on critical path (programs MOVE figuratives at runtime), but real CardDemo data layouts use figurative VALUE init widely.
acceptance_criteria: 01 WS-X PIC X(4) VALUE SPACES initializes WS-X to 4 spaces (0x40); VALUE ZEROS/LOW-VALUES/HIGH-VALUES fill correctly per field category; normal literal VALUEs and hex-literal VALUEs (red-dragon-3mx4) still encode correctly.
close_reason: VALUE HIGH-VALUES now emits raw 0xFF bytes via COBOL_RAW_FIGURATIVE_BYTES path in emit_encode_value; ZEROS and LOW-VALUES were already correct. 4 new integration tests added.

title: CICS: BMS symbolic map modeling (field <-> COBOL group suffixes I/O/L/A/F)
description: The BMS loader built in pz9g.5 models maps as flat offset+length fields only. Real BMS symbolic maps expose per-field COBOL subfields with name suffixes — input (I), output (O), length (L), attribute (A/F) — and CardDemo MOVEs to/from the suffixed names (e.g. an output field's ...O subfield). SEND/RECEIVE MAP must map each BMS field to the correct symbolic-map COBOL subfield so names line up with what the program references. The current flat byte-offset model cannot express this, so even after field-ref wiring (pz9g.7) the field names will not match.
design: Extend the BMS map model to carry the symbolic-map subfield structure per field. Loader should derive the symbolic group layout (or parse it from the generated copybook). SEND MAP reads each field's output subfield; RECEIVE MAP writes each field's input subfield. Decide whether to add the real external map-generation tool as a submodule or keep an enriched in-house model.
acceptance_criteria: SEND/RECEIVE MAP exchange data via the symbolic-map subfield names a CardDemo program actually references; covered by tests using a representative map.
notes: Design spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-07-cics-bms-symbolic-map-design.md
close_reason: BMS symbolic-map data flow: SEND reads <base>O, RECEIVE writes <base>I via vm.data_layout + WS region (mirrors EIB init); flat region model kept as fallback. Loader derives I/O/L subfield names. 129 CICS tests pass.

title: CICS audit: DFHRESP table completeness + verb coverage (LINK, TS queues, etc.)

Any other DFHRESP(name) the program references (e.g. DUPREC, NOTOPEN, LENGERR, INVREQ, DUPKEY) currently substitutes wrong/not at all -> parse error or wrong literal. Audit actual usage and bundle the full table. (2) Verb coverage: plans cover RETURN/XCTL/ABEND/ASSIGN/ASKTIME/FORMATTIME/INQUIRE/WRITEQ TD/HANDLE*/READ/WRITE/REWRITE/DELETE/STARTBR/READNEXT/READPREV/ENDBR/SEND MAP/RECEIVE MAP/SEND TEXT. Likely-needed but unplanned: LINK (call program + return, distinct from XCTL), READQ/WRITEQ/DELETEQ TS (temp storage, distinct from TD), RECEIVE (no map), SEND CONTROL, SYNCPOINT, GETMAIN/FREEMAIN, START/RETRIEVE. Audit which the target programs use and file follow-ups.

notes:
Design spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-07-cics-audit-dfhresp-verbs-design.md
AUDIT DONE (18 online programs). DFHRESP codes used: NORMAL, NOTFND, ENDFILE (have) + DUPREC, DUPKEY (missing) -> add these + full table + no-silent-miss guard. Verb coverage: NO gaps. No LINK, no TS queues (READQ/WRITEQ TS/DELETEQ), no interval-control START (all 21 START hits are STARTBR), no SYNCPOINT/GETMAIN. Everything used is covered by A-E + planned D. Minor verify: confirm a few bare RECEIVE are multi-line RECEIVE MAP, not keyboard RECEIVE.
close_reason: DFHRESP table completed: added DUPKEY=15 + full canonical 0-44 set + preserved higher codes; values verified unique. Unknown-condition fallback now substitutes a 9999 sentinel (never equals a real EIBRESP) instead of 0/NORMAL, so a typo'd condition can't masquerade as the normal path. Verb-coverage audit confirmed no gaps (no LINK/TS/START). 138 CICS tests pass.

title: CICS: BMS map runtime model (headless SEND/RECEIVE MAP)
description:
Backs SEND MAP / RECEIVE MAP — the screen layer of the online tier. Two halves:

(1) Map definitions (partly external): CardDemo ships 10 .bms screen sources (HLASM DFHMSD/DFHMDI/DFHMDF macros) plus generated symbolic copybooks (e.g. COSGN00.CPY with ...I input and ...O output field groups). The ~/code/bms-tools project (HLASM -> JSON -> COBOL symbolic copybook) is taking shape to generate these. Once generated, our existing DATA DIVISION machinery already handles the map records.

(2) Runtime model (this child): a headless representation of a map — fields, attributes, lengths — and SEND/RECEIVE semantics:
- RECEIVE MAP populates the symbolic ...I fields (and length/flag subfields) from supplied input.
- SEND MAP reads the symbolic ...O fields (+ ERASE/CURSOR/FREEKB options) into an output screen record.
- No real 3270 terminal required — represent the screen as a structured record the dispatch driver can feed/inspect.

Depends on bms-tools (or equivalent) for symbolic copybooks; coordinate so generated copybooks resolve via COPY. No decision here on terminal rendering — headless is sufficient for the fitness function.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A generated BMS symbolic copybook resolves via COPY and exposes ...I / ...O field groups. 2. RECEIVE MAP populates input fields from a supplied screen-input record. 3. SEND MAP reads output fields (with ERASE/CURSOR/FREEKB recognized) into an output record. 4. The sign-on map (COSGN00) round-trips: SEND then RECEIVE preserves field values headlessly.
close_reason: BMS screen engine complete: BmsLoader, SEND MAP/RECEIVE MAP/SEND TEXT builtins + lowering, symbolic-map data flow (pz9g.10), EIBAID write-back (pz9g.8). Exercised by real end-to-end flow in pz9g.9.

title: CICS: VSAM/KSDS file model behind CICS file control
description:
Backs the CICS file-control verbs (READ/WRITE/REWRITE/DELETE + browse STARTBR/READNEXT/READPREV/ENDBR). CardDemo online reads VSAM KSDS files (USRSEC user-security, accounts, cards, transactions) by key.

Semantics required (access-method level, independent of storage choice):
- KSDS = records keyed by primary key (RIDFLD). READ by exact key; RESP NORMAL/NOTFND.
- Browse cursor: STARTBR positions at/after a key; READNEXT/READPREV iterate in key order; ENDBR closes.
- WRITE (new key, DUPKEY if exists), REWRITE (update in place), DELETE (by key).
- File status / RESP mapping from each operation.
- Records load from CardDemo seed data (app/data EBCDIC/ASCII datasets).

IMPLEMENTATION APPROACH IS NOT DECIDED. Options to evaluate (do not pick here):
- Custom: back KSDS with an embedded ordered key->record store (sorted map / SQLite / B-tree); browse = range iteration over sorted keys. In-memory, deterministic, no external dep — likely fits a VM best.
- Open-source precedent: GnuCOBOL's indexed-file layer uses VBISAM (libvbisam, LGPL, C-ISAM compatible) or Berkeley DB (--with-db). KICKS (open CICS-alike) emulates VSAM by opening files per-transaction.
The choice (custom KV vs adapting an OSS ISAM lib) is a deliberate decision for when this child is scheduled; capture trade-offs (determinism, dependency weight, EBCDIC record handling) before committing.
acceptance_criteria: 1. KSDS READ by RIDFLD returns the keyed record into INTO; RESP NORMAL/NOTFND correct. 2. Browse STARTBR/READNEXT/READPREV iterate records in key order; ENDBR closes cleanly. 3. WRITE/REWRITE/DELETE mutate the dataset with correct RESP (incl. DUPKEY). 4. CardDemo seed data loads into the file model. 5. Implementation approach documented with trade-offs before coding.
close_reason: VSAM engine (SortedDict KSDS + FCT YAML), point ops (READ/WRITE/REWRITE/DELETE) and browse (STARTBR/READNEXT/READPREV/ENDBR) builtins + lowering. READ/READNEXT/READPREV fill the INTO buffer (Option A); all verbs write EIBRESP/RESP via F's copy-back. Real WRITE->READ and browse round-trips through run_cics. 122 CICS tests pass.
